title: Kanda Poha (Flattened Rice with Onion, Peanuts, Peas and Potato)
summary: Rinsed poha seasoned with turmeric, salt and sugar, folded into a tempering of peanuts, mustard and cumin seeds, curry leaves, chillies and onion with boiled potato and peas. Steamed briefly and finished with coriander and lemon.
equipment: large frying pan or kadai with lid

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
medium potato, boiled, peeled and diced

steps.title: Soften the poha
steps.text: Tip the poha into a sieve and rinse under cold water for about 30 seconds, tossing, until just softened but not mushy. Drain well, then toss with the turmeric, salt and sugar and leave for 5-10 min; the flakes absorb the clinging water and turn fluffy.

steps.title: Fry the peanuts
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat and fry the peanuts for 2-3 min until golden and crisp. Lift them out with a slotted spoon so they stay crunchy.

steps.title: Temper the spices
steps.text: Add the mustard seeds to the hot oil and, once they pop, the cumin, curry leaves and chillies for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 4-5 min until soft and translucent.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the potato and peas and cook for 2-3 min until heated through. Gently fold in the poha, cover and steam on low for 2-3 min, stirring once.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in most of the peanuts and coriander, scatter over the rest and serve hot with lemon wedges.

tips: Use thick poha; thin poha dissolves when rinsed.
Grated fresh coconut on top is a lovely addition.
Squeeze over the lemon just before eating to keep the colour bright.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate up to 1 day; sprinkle with water and reheat covered until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
